basis: Ordered species-specific profiles based on university extension sources. Genus-level information is labelled as such; cultivar-level claims remain limited to documented traits.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A rubber-tree cultivar selected for very dark burgundy foliage. Species-level care is supported by UF/IFAS; cultivar-specific differences beyond leaf color remain unverified.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Thick, leathery, broad oval leaves; 'Burgundy' is selected for deep maroon to nearly black coloration. Exact color varies with light and leaf age. Cultivar/hybrid-specific naming and diagnostic features remain under review; species or genus-level care should not be treated as proof of the exact horticultural identity.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright filtered light; acclimate gradually to stronger light and protect from hot afternoon sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Water thoroughly, then allow the upper layer of medium to dry. Do not leave roots standing in water.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Use a loose, moisture-retentive but well-drained potting medium and a pot with drainage holes.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; protect from cold drafts and chilling.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Average indoor humidity is usually tolerated; good airflow is more important than misting.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed a balanced houseplant fertilizer during active growth according to label directions; reduce feeding when growth slows.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Prune to control height or branching. Latex flows from cuts; use gloves and clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: UF/IFAS lists cuttings and layering as propagation approaches; use healthy stem sections and maintain warmth.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Ficus latex can irritate skin and eyes. Keep away from children and pets; avoid ingestion.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: UF/IFAS lists scale insects as an occasional problem. Yellow leaves may reflect excess water, poor light or root stress.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, filtered light and strong drainage are important. Check moisture more often in hot weather, but avoid saturated pots during monsoon periods.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical African evergreen tree commonly grown as a large indoor foliage specimen.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Large, thick, leathery, fiddle- or lyre-shaped leaves with prominent veins; milky sap is present in stems.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or partial shade; protect from harsh afternoon sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Allow the surface layer to dry slightly between thorough waterings. It is sensitive to overwatering.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Moist but well-drained loamy medium; avoid compacted soil and standing water.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; NC State recommends temperatures above 55°F (about 13°C).

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Medium humidity is suitable; maintain airflow and avoid persistent leaf wetness.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Balanced fertilizer during active growth, according to label; reduce feeding when growth slows.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Prune as needed to control size or remove damaged branches. Wear gloves because sap may irritate.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings are listed as a propagation strategy; use a viable node and warm rooting conditions.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Contains insoluble calcium oxalates; ingestion may cause oral irritation, drooling and vomiting. Keep away from pets and children.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Overwatering and poor drainage are key risks; sap may irritate skin. Watch for common scale and mite infestations.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: Maintain stable light and avoid moving the plant abruptly. In Dhaka, avoid hot direct balcony sun and water by soil condition.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: An evergreen tropical tree often trained as an indoor specimen or braided ornamental.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Slender arching branches, smooth grey trunk and glossy oval leaves; cultivars may have green or variegated foliage.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright light is needed for dense growth; avoid sudden changes in light and protect from intense afternoon sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Water thoroughly when the upper medium begins to dry; avoid both prolonged drought and waterlogging.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Well-drained, fertile potting mix in a container with drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; protect from cold drafts and abrupt temperature changes.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Average to moderately high humidity; dry air can contribute to leaf drop.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed during active growth with a balanced fertilizer according to label directions.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Prune to shape; young flexible stems can be trained or braided. Use clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Iowa State Extension lists Ficus benjamina among houseplants propagated by cuttings.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Ficus sap may irritate sensitive skin; ingestion may cause gastrointestinal upset. Keep away from pets and children.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Leaf drop can follow abrupt changes in light, watering or location. Check for scale and mites.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: Avoid frequent relocation. In Dhaka, ventilate well and check drainage during humid rainy periods.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical and subtropical Asian fig tree commonly trained as bonsai; the ginseng form is sold for its swollen exposed roots.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Small glossy dark-green leaves, grey bark and aerial roots. 'Ginseng' describes a horticultural form with swollen, exposed roots, not a separate species.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright light to sunny exposure; acclimate outdoor bonsai gradually to direct sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep evenly moist during active growth but allow excess water to drain. Avoid prolonged drying in a small bonsai pot.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Free-draining bonsai medium; use a shallow pot with open drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; NC State notes it is best kept above 68°F (20°C).

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity can encourage aerial-root development; maintain airflow.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth using a bonsai-appropriate balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Prune shoots to maintain bonsai form; latex is released from cuts, so use gloves and clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings are a documented propagation method; grafting is also used in horticulture.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Ficus latex may irritate skin; keep away from pets and children and do not ingest.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Scale and other bonsai pests may occur; inspect branches, leaf undersides and roots. Avoid waterlogged soil.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, protect bonsai from scorching midday sun and heavy rain; do not let shallow pots dry completely.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical wetland-edge tree from Central and South America, widely grown as a braided-stem indoor money tree.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Palmately compound leaves with several leaflets radiating from one point; often sold with braided trunks.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; it tolerates some shade but grows better with good light.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Water when the upper medium begins to dry; keep evenly moist but never waterlogged.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Rich, moisture-retentive but well-drained medium; container must drain freely.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; protect from cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Moderate to high humidity is suitable; maintain airflow.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed modestly during active growth with a balanced houseplant fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Prune to maintain canopy shape; braided stems are a nursery training technique, not a natural growth form.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings and seed are possible for the species; household propagation success can vary.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: NC State notes possible toxicity from seeds if ingested; houseplants rarely produce seeds. Keep seeds away from people and pets.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Overwatering and poor drainage can cause root problems; monitor for scale and mites.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, avoid waterlogged pots during monsoon weather and provide bright filtered light.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A compact evergreen shrub from Taiwan, commonly sold under the former name Schefflera arboricola.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Palmately compound leaves with several glossy leaflets radiating from a central point; dwarf form branches readily.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; tolerates some shade but variegated forms need brighter filtered light.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Water when the upper portion of the medium begins to dry; do not leave the roots saturated.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Well-drained general-purpose potting mix with organic matter.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm indoor conditions; protect from cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Average indoor humidity is tolerated; good airflow is beneficial.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed during active growth with a balanced fertilizer following the label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Pinch or prune stems to maintain a compact shape; use gloves if sap irritates skin.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings are a common propagation method for dwarf umbrella tree.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Schefflera/Heptapleurum is listed as toxic in UConn's houseplant safety reference. Keep away from pets and children.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Watch for scale, mealybugs and spider mites; overwatering can cause root decline.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, give bright filtered light and adjust watering to actual drying rather than a fixed weekly schedule.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical evergreen shrub grown for brightly colored foliage; it needs more light and warmth than many low-light houseplants.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Leaves vary widely in shape and show combinations of green, yellow, orange, red and purple; cultivar variation is substantial.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Give very bright filtered light or gentle morning sun to maintain color; acclimate gradually and protect from intense midday heat.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium evenly moist during active growth but allow excess water to drain. Avoid prolonged drying and waterlogging.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Rich, well-drained medium with organic matter.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; protect from cold and drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity supports foliage quality; provide airflow to reduce fungal risk.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label; avoid excessive salts.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Prune to shape or remove damaged stems. Wear gloves because milky sap can irritate.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings are a documented houseplant propagation approach.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Croton sap is irritating and the plant is harmful if ingested. Keep away from children and pets; wear gloves.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Leaf drop can follow cold, low light or abrupt changes. Watch for scale, mealybugs and spider mites.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, bright morning light may be useful, but protect from extreme afternoon heat and heavy rain exposure.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical evergreen shrub or small tree from the western Pacific and Southeast Asian region, grown for colorful foliage.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Upright woody cane with rosettes of long strap-like leaves; colors vary by cultivar from green to pink, red and purple.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright filtered light; stronger light can intensify color, but protect from harsh midday sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep the medium evenly moist but well drained; reduce watering if growth slows.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Rich, moisture-retentive, well-drained potting mix.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; protect from cold.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Moderate to high humidity; maintain good airflow.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove old leaves and prune canes to control height; new shoots may emerge below cuts.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem or cane cuttings are commonly used; ensure each section has viable nodes.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Some Cordyline species are toxic to pets; confirm the specific species and keep away from animals until safety is established.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Potential issues include leaf spotting, scale and spider mites; avoid stagnant, wet foliage.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, protect from scorching sun and ensure drainage during monsoon rains.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A slow-growing tropical shrub or small tree; the Song of India trade form is valued for narrow variegated foliage.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Woody stems carry dense spirals of narrow lance-shaped leaves. Song of India typically has green leaves with cream margins; catalog identity should be checked against the actual plant.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; variegated forms need sufficient filtered light to maintain contrast.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium lightly moist but allow the top layer to dry between waterings. Avoid overwatering.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Loose, well-drained potting mix; adding perlite or coarse material improves drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: NC State gives 65–75°F (18–24°C) as preferred conditions for D. reflexa var. reflexa; protect from cold.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity is preferred; provide airflow and avoid wet foliage.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed modestly during active growth using balanced fertilizer; reduce feeding when growth slows.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove damaged leaves and prune stems to control shape; use clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings can be used for propagation; keep cuttings warm and lightly moist.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Dracaena contains saponins and can cause illness if ingested, particularly in cats and dogs. Keep away from pets and children.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Sensitive to fluoride and chlorine in tap water; brown tips may also reflect low humidity or salt build-up. Watch for scale and mealybugs.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, use filtered or rain water if tap-water tip burn is recurrent; keep plants ventilated in humid months.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A slow-growing tropical African shrub grown indoors for its cane-like trunk and broad strap-shaped foliage.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Tall woody cane with a crown of broad linear-lanceolate leaves; cultivars may have central yellow or white stripes.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright to moderate filtered light; direct sun can burn foliage, while very low light produces narrower leaves.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium lightly moist during active growth; allow the surface to dry somewhat and reduce watering when growth slows.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Commercial potting mix with good drainage; use a container with drainage holes.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: NC State says 70–80°F (21–27°C) is favorable and advises keeping above 50°F (10°C).

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Moderate humidity; brown tips may occur in dry air or from salts in water.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed modestly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove old leaves and prune canes to manage height; cuttings can be used to restart or branch plants.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings are a documented propagation method.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Contains saponins; ingestion may cause mouth and stomach irritation, vomiting and drooling in people and pets. Keep away from cats and dogs.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Susceptible to thrips and mealybugs; sensitive to fluoride and salt build-up causing brown tips.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, use filtered water if leaf tips brown, keep in bright filtered light and ventilate during monsoon.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical West African shrub commonly sold as lucky bamboo, although it is not a true bamboo.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Green cane-like stems with narrow leaves; stems are often trained into spirals or braids.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or partial shade; avoid direct hot sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Can grow in moist potting mix or chlorine-free water. If grown in water, change it weekly and keep roots submerged, not the whole stem.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Use a moist but well-drained potting mix, or a clean water vessel with pebbles supporting the roots.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm indoor conditions; protect from cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Average to moderate humidity; low humidity may brown leaf tips.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: If grown in water, use only weak liquid fertilizer sparingly; overfeeding can damage roots. Follow label directions.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove yellow leaves and trim canes with clean tools; avoid cutting below healthy nodes without purpose.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings can root in water or moist medium; ensure nodes are present.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Dracaena contains saponins and may be harmful if ingested by pets. Keep away from cats and dogs.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Overwatering can yellow leaves and rot stems; watch for mealybugs, mites and scale. Stagnant water may breed mosquitoes.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, change water weekly, keep containers clean and out of direct sun; check for mosquito larvae.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tender tuberous tropical perennial grown for colorful foliage; it naturally has a seasonal growth and rest cycle.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Arrowhead-shaped, peltate leaves on long upright petioles, with highly variable white, pink, red and green patterns.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Partial shade to filtered light; many cultivars lose color intensity in strong direct sun. Some tolerate gentle morning sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep soil consistently moist while actively growing; this is a moisture-demanding plant, but the medium must still drain.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Fertile, acidic, high-organic-matter medium with good drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions are essential for active growth; cold can trigger dormancy and leaf dieback.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity supports foliage, but airflow is important to reduce rot.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: NC State recommends regular feeding during active growth; use balanced fertilizer according to label rather than copying landscape rates into a pot.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove yellowing leaves at the base; do not damage the tuber.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Propagate by dividing tubers or offsets, ensuring each division has a viable bud.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Caladium is poisonous if eaten, with medium severity listed by NC State. Keep away from children and pets.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Slugs and snails can damage leaves; tuber or root rot can occur in cold or waterlogged conditions.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, maintain moisture in active hot-season growth but protect tubers from prolonged waterlogging during monsoon periods.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: The trade plant commonly called Alocasia Polly is a cultivated hybrid, not a naturally occurring species. The exact parentage and cultivar naming are inconsistently presented in horticultural trade.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Compact upright plant with dark arrow-shaped leaves, prominent pale veins and wavy margins. The catalog identity should be treated as a horticultural hybrid rather than a confirmed botanical species. Cultivar/hybrid-specific naming and diagnostic features remain under review; species or genus-level care should not be treated as proof of the exact horticultural identity.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; avoid harsh direct sun that can scorch leaves.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium evenly moist during active growth but never saturated. Allow the upper surface to begin drying before watering again.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Airy, moisture-retentive aroid medium with excellent drainage; avoid compacted soil.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; protect from cold and sudden temperature changes.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity is helpful, but combine it with airflow to reduce leaf disease.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label; reduce or pause when growth slows.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove dead leaves at the base with clean tools; avoid damaging the corm.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Division of offsets or corms is used for Alocasia propagation; do not divide a plant without viable growth points.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Alocasia contains calcium oxalate crystals and is harmful if eaten; sap can irritate. Keep away from children and pets.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Root and corm rot can follow overwatering; inspect for spider mites and mealybugs. Leaf yellowing may also accompany dormancy or stress.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, maintain warmth and airflow; during monsoon, drainage is more important than increasing watering frequency.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical Alocasia grown for its upright, patterned stems and large arrow-shaped foliage.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Distinctive zebra-striped petioles support green arrow-shaped leaves; stems are a key feature distinguishing it from other Alocasia.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or filtered shade; avoid scorching direct sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium evenly moist in active growth but not soggy. Allow slight surface drying between waterings.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Rich, airy, well-drained medium; maintain moisture without waterlogging.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; protect from cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity is beneficial with good ventilation.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed modestly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove old leaves at the base; handle petioles carefully as they can be brittle.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Propagate by division of offsets or corms when present.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Alocasia contains calcium oxalate crystals; ingestion causes oral irritation. Keep away from children and pets.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Root rot in wet media and spider mites in dry/stressed conditions are possible; inspect before treating.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, avoid prolonged exposure to heavy rain and ensure the pot drains freely.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A very large tropical elephant-ear perennial grown for its huge foliage and cormous growth.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Massive sagittate leaves on stout petioles; mature plants can become several metres tall in suitable outdoor conditions.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Full sun to partial shade depending on acclimation and water supply; container plants benefit from protection from extreme afternoon heat.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep consistently moist during active growth; it tolerates wetter conditions than many houseplants but roots still need oxygen.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Rich, moisture-retentive soil with organic matter; ensure excess water can drain in containers.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; growth slows in cool weather.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity is naturally suitable; maintain airflow around large leaves.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label; large fast-growing plants may use nutrients quickly.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove damaged or senescent leaves with clean tools; sap can irritate.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Corm offsets or division are used for propagation; ensure each piece has a viable bud.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Alocasia contains calcium oxalate crystals and is harmful if raw plant parts are eaten. Keep away from children and pets.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Wind can tear leaves; corm rot can occur in stagnant water. Monitor for mites and sap-feeding pests.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, protect large leaves from strong wind and support drainage during monsoon rainfall.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical corm-forming perennial known as taro or elephant ear, grown for very large leaves and sometimes as a food crop.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Large heart- or shield-shaped leaves with the petiole attached near the centre of the blade; clumping plants arise from corms.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Part shade to full sun depending on water availability; protect container foliage from harsh wind and scorching conditions.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Requires abundant moisture and should not be allowed to dry out during active growth. Maintain moist soil, not stagnant anaerobic conditions in a pot.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Rich, moisture-retentive soil; unlike many aroids, Colocasia tolerates wetter conditions, but container roots still need oxygen.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm tropical conditions; cold slows growth and can cause dieback.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity suits the plant; allow air movement around leaves.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label; fast growth requires nutrients.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove old leaves at the base; use gloves if sap causes irritation.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Propagate by dividing corms or offsets with viable growing points.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Raw taro tissues contain irritating calcium oxalate crystals; food use requires proper preparation and cooking. Do not eat ornamental plants unless correctly identified and safely prepared.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Leaf damage from wind and root/corm rot in stagnant containers are possible. Inspect for chewing pests.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, it can grow vigorously in warm weather; keep moist but avoid sealed, stagnant pots and overflowing saucers.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical rainforest understory perennial formerly known as Calathea orbifolia, grown for its broad patterned leaves.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Large, rounded green leaves with broad silver-green bands; leaves emerge from a clumping rhizomatous base.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or partial shade; direct sun can scorch leaves.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep consistently moist but never soggy. Use rainwater or distilled water where tap-water fluoride causes brown tips.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Moist, well-drained, slightly acidic mix; avoid drying completely and avoid waterlogging.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: NC State gives 65–75°F (18–24°C) as a preferred range; avoid cold drafts and temperature swings.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity of at least 60% is recommended by NC State; airflow remains essential.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed monthly during active growth with a diluted balanced liquid fertilizer; reduce when growth slows.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove damaged leaves at the base with clean scissors.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Division of rhizomes is the practical propagation method.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: No significant toxicity warning was found in the cited NC State profile; do not infer safety for every pet or individual.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Brown tips can result from fluoride, low humidity or inconsistent moisture. Watch for spider mites and fungal problems in stagnant air.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, high ambient humidity may help, but maintain airflow and use rain/filtered water if leaf tips brown.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical Brazilian rainforest perennial formerly called Calathea insignis, grown as a foliage houseplant.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Narrow wavy leaves with alternating dark and light green oval markings and purple undersides; clumping fountain-like habit.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or partial shade; avoid direct sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium consistently moist but not soggy; water when the surface begins to dry slightly.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Peat-based or African-violet style mix with organic matter and good drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm stable temperatures; avoid cold drafts and abrupt changes.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity is preferred; ensure airflow to prevent fungal leaf issues.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Use diluted balanced liquid fertilizer during active growth according to label; reduce during slow growth.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove damaged leaves at the base; avoid tearing healthy stems.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Division of established clumps is the usual propagation method for Goeppertia.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: No specific toxicity claim is made from the reviewed source; keep plants away from pets until species-specific safety is confirmed.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Leaf edge browning may reflect low humidity, water quality or inconsistent moisture; mites may occur.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: Dhaka humidity may be adequate, but ventilation and filtered light are important, especially in rainy months.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical rainforest understory perennial formerly called Calathea ornata, grown for its decorative pinstriped foliage.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Dark green leaves with thin pinkish-white stripes on the upper surface and purple undersides; erect clumping habit.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or partial shade; direct sun can fade or scorch foliage.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep medium evenly moist but not soggy; do not allow complete drying.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Moist, well-drained peat-based or African-violet potting mix.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm stable conditions; protect from cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: High humidity is preferred; provide good air movement.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Monthly balanced liquid fertilizer during active growth, diluted and applied according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove old leaves at the base with clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Division of clumps is the common propagation method; seed propagation not confirmed here.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Toxicity was not established by the source reviewed for this profile; do not assume pet safety without confirmation.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Brown edges may follow low humidity, hard water or dry medium; avoid stagnant wet foliage.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, monitor drainage and airflow; don't compensate for brown tips by keeping roots constantly wet.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical creeping perennial in the prayer-plant family, grown for patterned foliage and its daily leaf movement.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Oval leaves with contrasting veins and markings; leaves fold upward at night and reopen in daylight, a nyctinastic movement.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or partial shade; avoid direct sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep evenly moist but not waterlogged. Allow only slight surface drying before watering again.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Moisture-retentive, airy, slightly acidic medium with good drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm stable conditions; avoid cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Moderate to high humidity is beneficial; maintain airflow.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly with balanced fertilizer during active growth according to label; reduce in slow periods.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Pinch growing tips to encourage a fuller plant; remove damaged leaves.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings with nodes or division of rooted clumps are common methods; verify cultivar-specific details separately.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: No specific toxicity conclusion is asserted here; verify the exact species before treating as pet-safe.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Dry edges can reflect low humidity, mineral-rich water or inconsistent moisture; watch for spider mites.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, avoid hot direct sun and stagnant wet soil; maintain steady moisture and ventilation.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A compact tropical evergreen herb from South America, often called baby rubber plant but unrelated to Ficus elastica.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Glossy, thick, spoon-shaped or obovate leaves; branched stems and pink-tinged petioles are useful identification features.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; tolerates lower light for a time but avoid strong direct sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Allow the medium to dry between waterings; it dislikes both wet soil and severe prolonged drought.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Very well-drained, airy mix; a succulent-style blend can help avoid water retention.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm indoor conditions; avoid cold drafts.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Medium to low humidity is tolerated; high humidity is not required.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Pinch or trim stems to maintain a compact shape.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Leaf or stem cuttings are used for propagation; use healthy material and allow wounds to dry briefly if rooting in mix.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: No specific toxicity warning is reported in the reviewed NC State profile; do not generalize this to all Peperomia species without checking.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Overwatering causes yellowing and root rot; monitor for mealybugs, spider mites and whiteflies.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, prioritize airy soil and let the pot dry between waterings, especially in monsoon humidity.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A compact tropical Peperomia grown for its watermelon-like leaf pattern.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Nearly round, peltate leaves with alternating silver and dark-green bands radiating from the petiole attachment; reddish petioles are common.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; protect from direct hot sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Water when the upper medium has dried; avoid waterlogged roots. Its fleshy leaves store some moisture.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Airy, well-drained mix with organic matter and added aeration.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; protect from cold.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Average indoor humidity is usually sufficient; good airflow is more important than misting.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth using balanced fertilizer at label strength or weaker.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Remove damaged leaves and pinch leggy growth with clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Leaf or petiole cuttings and division may be used; ensure a viable growing point is present.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: No specific toxicity statement is made here because the source reviewed did not provide one.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Overwatering and root rot are key risks for Peperomia; inspect for mealybugs and mites.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, allow the mix to dry appropriately and protect from direct afternoon sun and heavy rain.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical foliage plant grown for colorful speckled leaves, commonly called polka dot plant.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Opposite oval leaves marked with pink, red, white or other contrasting spots over green; color depends on cultivar.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light; adequate light helps maintain compact growth and color, but avoid harsh direct sun.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep evenly moist but well drained; do not allow repeated severe wilting or waterlogging.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Moisture-retentive but airy potting mix with good drainage.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; protect from cold and temperature swings.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Higher humidity supports foliage; maintain airflow.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Pinch tips regularly to maintain a bushy habit and delay flowering/legginess.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings root readily in moist medium or water; seed may also be used.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Toxicity is not established by the cited source for this entry; do not assume pet safety without a reliable toxicology reference.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Plants can become leggy if light is inadequate or pruning is neglected; watch for aphids and whiteflies.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, keep evenly moist in active growth but avoid waterlogging; pinch often in warm weather.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A tropical perennial widely grown as an ornamental foliage plant, with many cultivars selected for leaf color and pattern.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Opposite leaves with scalloped or toothed margins; foliage color ranges widely. Cultivar variation is substantial.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright filtered light or gentle morning sun; light needs vary among cultivars, and harsh sun can scorch some selections.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep evenly moist but well drained during active growth; avoid prolonged drought in small pots.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Fertile, moisture-retentive but well-drained potting mix.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; growth declines in cool weather.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Moderate humidity is suitable; airflow helps reduce foliar disease.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed lightly during active growth; avoid excessive nitrogen that can encourage soft growth and reduce color quality.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Pinch growing tips and remove flower spikes if maintaining foliage form; prune with clean tools.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings root readily in water or moist medium; seed may not reproduce named cultivars true to type.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Toxicity varies by species/cultivar and reliable pet-safety evidence was not established for this profile; keep away from pets until verified.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Watch for mealybugs, aphids, whiteflies and downy mildew in humid stagnant conditions.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, provide morning light and afternoon protection; prune regularly and maintain airflow in monsoon weather.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: A trailing or spreading tropical perennial grown for purple foliage and fast growth.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Succulent-like purple stems with pointed, lance-shaped leaves; color is strongest in good light.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright light to some direct sun after gradual acclimation; more light usually deepens purple coloration, but extreme afternoon heat can scorch.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Allow the upper medium to dry somewhat between waterings; avoid prolonged saturation.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Well-drained potting mix; it tolerates relatively lean, airy media.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: Warm conditions; protect from cold.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: Average humidity is tolerated; avoid stagnant air and wet foliage.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Feed sparingly during active growth with balanced fertilizer according to label.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: Pinch or prune stems to keep compact; cuttings can be used to fill bare areas.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: Stem cuttings root easily in water or moist medium; nodes are essential.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Sap may irritate skin in sensitive people; avoid eye contact and wash after handling. Confirm pet-specific safety before assuming harmlessness.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: Overwatering can cause stem or root rot; watch for mites and leaf spotting in stagnant conditions.

sections.title: Seasonal care
sections.content: In Dhaka, it can grow quickly in warm light; protect from extreme afternoon heat and trim often.
